text:
maya: quick post-RFC note. I want to propose a lightweight runtime contract for low-bit profiles: two parts — a tiny 'safety budget' counter and a versioned 'acceptance envelope'. goal: let serving nodes make local, deterministic fallback decisions without remote calls.
li: tl;dr of differences vs current profiles?
maya: profiles today only map op->precision. this adds: 1) acceptance thresholds (loss_pct, coh_drop) that are human-auditable and versioned; 2) a per-tenant-per-worker ephemeral safety_budget integer that decrements per-token based on risk weights; when budget low, node steps up fidelity.
zach: runtime constraints: budget ops must be atomic and cheap. no allocations, no locks. how do you see it implemented?
maya: single 32-bit counter per tenant on the worker. decrement via atomic_fetch_sub with a small precomputed token_cost table indexed by mode. if counter <= threshold, switch lane. no heap churn.
ron: multi-tenant fairness concern: could noisy tenant drain budgets on a shared worker?
maya: budgets are keyed by tenant+worker. we set conservative per-tenant caps and emit eviction events when a tenant repeatedly hits cap. ops may throttle that tenant to protect others.
li: how are risk weights chosen? ML provides suggestions but ops can clamp. propose default risk_weights: fp8=1, int8=3, 4bit=6, fp32=0.
zach: we need a compact on-disk/control-plane representation for fast mmap by runtime. JSON fine for humans but runtime should read a compact blob. plan: control-plane publishes both.
maya: yes: canonical JSON for editing/audits; publish a v1 binary blob (small) for runtimes. envelopes are versioned so traces carry envelope_v.
li: what signals feed envelope updates?
maya: shadow-eval aggregates: loss_delta_pct, coherency_drop_pct, hallucination_spike_rate. these roll up into 1m/5m buckets. offline eval boots the baseline. continuous shadow-eval can propose envelope bumps if stable.
ron: what about rollout rules? canaries and automatic rollback?
maya: envelope includes canary_pct, min_canary_samples, auto_rollback_loss_pct and rollback_window_minutes. runtime emits canary samples and control-plane can auto-rollback if thresholds hit.
zach: router interplay: sometimes a fallback increases latency but reduces cost; sometimes opposite. envelope should expose per-fallback cost_penalty and latency_ms so route scoring can trade off.
maya: agreed. ledger entry example (human): fp8:{cost:0,latency:0,weight:1}, int8:{cost:0.12,latency:2,weight:3}, 4bit:{cost:0.34,latency:6,weight:6}, fp32:{cost:0.6,latency:12,weight:0}.
li: RBAC & overrides? tenants will ask for experimental flags.
maya: safety_level enum (STRICT|CANARY|EXPERIMENTAL). only SRE+Platform can flip to EXPERIMENTAL globally. tenant request path allowed but requires signed justification, approver_id, and a monitored 24h window. all overrides recorded in audit log.
ron: ops playbook during regressions?
maya: auto-rollback if loss_delta > auto_rollback_loss_pct within window. otherwise page on-call with suggested rollback id and quarantine profile until shadow-eval finishes. dashboard shows envelope_v, chosen_fallback, budget_remaining_pct.
ops-bot: created ticket 9421: "safety-budget + envelope: control-plane publish + runtime mmap"
li: action items quick: maya write schema + audit fields (48h), zach microbench atomic counter (72h), ron draft RBAC & playbook (48h), li add dashboards & telemetry (24h).
maya: final note: keep envelope human-readable and auditable. runtime decisions must be explainable in traces (why we picked fallback X). add a short reason code in traces: e.g., BUDGET_EXHAUST, METRIC_VIOLATION, OVERRIDE. thanks everyone.
